why: FIVE STATES. THE FIRST TWO EXIST BECAUSE EVERY ARM THAT WRITES THIS UNIT'S
TWO PRINCIPAL OUTPUTS NEEDS A TRIPLE, WHICH R6's ALL-PAIRS FALLBACK CANNOT
REACH; the last three exist because three of the four shutdown triggers never
fire in any scenario this campaign runs.
This is unit #37's finding met a second time, and the generator's own
coverage line says so:
283 combination(s) of the 10 quantit(y/ies) ... ALL PAIRS ONLY
-- the full cross product is 186624, past the 4096 bound
and under all-pairs every knob not being crossed sits at its ladder's FIRST
value. `CntrPar_SD_Method`'s ladder is [0, 1, 2, 3], so its first value is 0
-- neither of the two methods. Reaching the statement
LocalVar%SD_MaxPitchRate = CntrPar%SD_MaxPitchRate(LocalVar%SD_Stage)
needs SD_Method in {1,2} AND SD_Stage /= 0 AND SD_Stage <= SD_Stage_N, three
quantities at once. The first sweep measured the cost exactly: 29 of 109
mutants survived, and every survivor that is not an equivalence lives on one
of those arms --
arith_op       'SD_Stage - 1' -> 'SD_Stage + 1'          x3
swap_operands  'SD_Stage - 1' -> '1 - SD_Stage'          x6
swap_operands  'I_Stage - 1'  -> '1 - I_Stage'           x1
-- the subscripts of the four SD_ allocatables, which no case reached.
SD_Stage IS 2 AND NOT 1 IN BOTH STATES, and that is unit #38's rule rather
than a preference: at SD_Stage = 1 the expressions `SD_Stage - 1` and
`1 - SD_Stage` are the SAME NUMBER, so a corpus that only ever presents 1
cannot kill the swap no matter how many cases it runs. SD_Stage_N is 2 so
that stage 2 is inside the `.LE.` arm, and every SD_ array is longer than
that, so R11's own walk of SD_Stage over [0, 1, 2] stays in bounds.
R5's ARRAY-ELEMENTS-DISTINCT RULE IS OBSERVED: all four SD_ ramps below have
a non-zero step. Unit #38's first baseline wrote a constant ramp for two
index arrays and made ten index mutants unkillable; with every element equal,
`A[i-1]` and `A[1-i]` return the same number and the mutant is invisible.
THE TIME QUANTITIES ARE SET SO THAT THE STAGE CLOCK DECIDES SOMETHING.
Method 1's second arm advances the stage when
Time >= SD_StageStartTime + SD_StageTime(SD_Stage)
and with Time = 400, SD_StageStartTime = 100 and SD_StageTime(2) = 250 the
sum is 350, so the arm fires -- while SD_StageTime(1) = 200 gives 300, which
also fires, and SD_StageTime(3) = 300 gives 400, which is the EQUALITY. So
R11's walk of SD_Stage over its three values crosses the predicate's boundary
rather than sitting on one side of it.
Time = 400 is also past SD_TimeActivate = 300 and past SD_Time = 350, so the
trigger window is open and the SD_EnableTime arm fires -- which is the ONLY
one of the four triggers scenario 9 ever reaches, and the three that it does
not are then reached by R11 walking each SD_Enable* knob off this state.
objInst%instLPF IS NAMED because an unnamed varied parameter is inert-filled
to 0, and 0 is not an admissible filter slot: LPFilter would subscript
element -1 of six DIMENSION(1024) arrays. Same bound as harness/ranges.toml's
-- see the [Shutdown] block there and evidence/Shutdown/harness.case21_probe.txt.
THREE MORE STATES, ONE PER TRIGGER THAT SCENARIO 9 NEVER FIRES. The four
trigger tests are four independent IFs, not an ELSEIF chain, so when more
than one condition holds the LAST one wins and the earlier constants are
unobservable. Coverage records SD_Trigger = 1, 2 and 3 at ZERO hits in all 27
scenarios against one hit for SD_Trigger = 4, and the first mutation sweep
reproduced that from the other side: `const_tweak '2' -> '3'` survived 14,253
cases. Each state below enables exactly one trigger and puts its threshold
beyond reach on the true side, so the constant that arm writes is the value
the call returns.

states.name: method1_inside_the_stage_arm
states.why: SD_Method=1 with SD_Stage=2 inside SD_Stage_N=2, so the second arm runs: it subscripts SD_MaxPitchRate, SD_MaxTorqueRate and SD_StageTime with SD_Stage, and its stage-advance predicate sits one step either side of equality as R11 walks SD_Stage.

states.name: method2_inside_the_pitch_search
states.why: SD_Method=2 with SD_Stage=2, so the ELSE arm runs its DO I_Stage = 1, SD_Stage_N search over SD_StagePitch and then subscripts the two rate arrays. BlPitchCMeas=0.15 sits between SD_StagePitch(1)=0.1 and SD_StagePitch(2)=0.19, so the loop's predicate has both answers inside one call and the LAST index that matches -- not the first -- is what decides the stage.

states.name: only_the_pitch_trigger
states.why: SD_EnablePitch=1 and the other three 0, with SD_MaxPit at -1e6 so the filtered pitch exceeds it whatever LPFilter returns. The four trigger tests are four independent IFs in source order, so the LAST one that fires wins -- and with only this one enabled, SD_Trigger ends at 1 and the constant 1 is observable. In scenario 9 this arm runs 0 times in 11,999 calls.

states.name: only_the_yaw_trigger
states.why: SD_EnableYawError=1 alone, SD_MaxYawError=-1.0 so ABS(SD_NacVaneF) > it for every value including zero. This is the ONLY trigger whose threshold cannot be reached by R6's relational-pair rule: SD_BlPitchF and SD_GenSpeedF are LocalVar fields the generator varies as inputs, so it can set SD_MaxPit and SD_MaxGenSpd FROM them, but SD_NacVaneF is written from wrap_180(atan2(...)) inside the body and no input names it. 0 hits in all 27 scenarios.

states.name: only_the_genspeed_trigger
states.why: SD_EnableGenSpeed=1 alone, SD_MaxGenSpd=-1e6. SD_Trigger ends at 3. 0 hits in all 27 scenarios.
